L165: # Public Rest API for Binance SPOT Testnet
L166: ## General API Information
L167:   * The base endpoint is cite42†https://testnet.binance.vision/api†testnet.binance.vision L168:   * Responses are in JSON by default. To receive responses in SBE, refer to the cite43†SBE FAQ page.
L169:   * Data is returned in chronological order, unless noted otherwise.
L170:     * Without `startTime` or `endTime`, returns the most recent items up to the limit.
L171:     * With `startTime`, returns oldest items from `startTime` up to the limit.
L172:     * With `endTime`, returns most recent items up to `endTime` and the limit.
L173:     * With both, behaves like `startTime` but does not exceed `endTime`.
L174:   * All time and timestamp related fields in the JSON responses are in milliseconds by default. To receive the information in microseconds, please add the header `X-MBX-TIME-UNIT:MICROSECOND` or `X-MBX-TIME-UNIT:microsecond`.
L175:   * We support HMAC, RSA, and Ed25519 keys. For more information, please see cite44†API Key types .
L176:   * Timestamp parameters (e.g. `startTime`, `endTime`, `timestamp`) can be passed in milliseconds or microseconds.
L177:   * If there are enums or terms you want clarification on, please see the cite45†SPOT Glossary for more information.
L178:   * APIs have a timeout of 10 seconds when processing a request. If a response from the Matching Engine takes longer than this, the API responds with "Timeout waiting for response from backend server. Send status unknown; execution status unknown." cite46†(-1007 TIMEOUT) L179:     * This does not always mean that the request failed in the Matching Engine.
L180:     * If the status of the request has not appeared in cite36†User Data Stream , please perform an API query for its status.
L181:   * Please avoid SQL keywords in requests as they may trigger a security block by a WAF (Web Application Firewall) rule. See cite47†https://www.binance.com/en/support/faq/detail/360004492232†www.binance.com for more details.
L182:   * If your request contains a symbol name containing non-ASCII characters, then the response may contain non-ASCII characters encoded in UTF-8.
L183:   * Some endpoints may return asset and/or symbol names containing non-ASCII characters encoded in UTF-8 even if the request did not contain non-ASCII characters.
L184: ## HTTP Return Codes
L185:   * HTTP `4XX` return codes are used for malformed requests; the issue is on the sender's side.
L186:   * HTTP `403` return code is used when a WAF (Web Application Firewall) rule has been violated. This can indicate a rate limit violation or a security block. See cite47†https://www.binance.com/en/support/faq/detail/360004492232†www.binance.com for more details.
L187:   * HTTP `409` return code is used when a cancelReplace order partially succeeds. (i.e. if the cancellation of the order fails but the new order placement succeeds.)
L188:   * HTTP `429` return code is used when breaking a request rate limit.
L189:   * HTTP `418` return code is used when an IP has been auto-banned for continuing to send requests after receiving `429` codes.
L190:   * HTTP `5XX` return codes are used for internal errors; the issue is on Binance's side. It is important to NOT treat this as a failure operation; the execution status is UNKNOWN and could have been a success.
L191: ## Error Codes
L192: 
L193:   * Any endpoint can return an ERROR
L194: 
L195: Sample Payload below:
L196: 
L197:     Code
L198: 
L199:     `{
L200:         "code": -1121,
L201:         "msg": "Invalid symbol."
L202:     }`
L203: 
L204:   * Specific error codes and messages are defined in cite29†Errors Codes .
L205: ## General Information on Endpoints
L206:   * For `GET` endpoints, parameters must be sent as a `query string`.
L207:   * For `POST`, `PUT`, and `DELETE` endpoints, the parameters may be sent as a `query string` or in the `request body` with content type `application/x-www-form-urlencoded`. You may mix parameters between both the `query string` and `request body` if you wish to do so.
L208:   * Parameters may be sent in any order.
L209:   * If a parameter sent in both the `query string` and `request body`, the `query string` parameter will be used.
L210: ## LIMITS
L211: ### General Info on Limits
L212:   * The following `intervalLetter` values for headers:
L213:     * SECOND => S
L214:     * MINUTE => M
L215:     * HOUR => H
L216:     * DAY => D
L217:   * `intervalNum` describes the amount of the interval. For example, `intervalNum` 5 with `intervalLetter` M means "Every 5 minutes".
L218:   * The `/api/v3/exchangeInfo` `rateLimits` array contains objects related to the exchange's `RAW_REQUESTS`, `REQUEST_WEIGHT`, and `ORDERS` rate limits. These are further defined in the `ENUM definitions` section under `Rate limiters (rateLimitType)`.
L219:   * Requests fail with HTTP status code 429 when you exceed the request rate limit.
L220: ### IP Limits
L221:   * Every request will contain `X-MBX-USED-WEIGHT-(intervalNum)(intervalLetter)` in the response headers which has the current used weight for the IP for all request rate limiters defined.
L222:   * Each route has a `weight` which determines for the number of requests each endpoint counts for. Heavier endpoints and endpoints that do operations on multiple symbols will have a heavier `weight`.
L223:   * When a 429 is received, it's your obligation as an API to back off and not spam the API.
L224:   * Repeatedly violating rate limits and/or failing to back off after receiving 429s will result in an automated IP ban (HTTP status 418).
L225:   * IP bans are tracked and scale in duration for repeat offenders, from 2 minutes to 3 days.
L226:   * A `Retry-After` header is sent with a 418 or 429 responses and will give the number of seconds required to wait, in the case of a 429, to prevent a ban, or, in the case of a 418, until the ban is over.
L227:   * The limits on the API are based on the IPs, not the API keys.
L228: ### Unfilled Order Count
L229:   * Every successful order response will contain a `X-MBX-ORDER-COUNT-(intervalNum)(intervalLetter)` header indicating how many orders you have placed for that interval. To monitor this, refer to cite48†`GET api/v3/rateLimit/order` .
L230:   * Rejected/unsuccessful orders are not guaranteed to have `X-MBX-ORDER-COUNT-**` headers in the response.
L231:   * If you have exceeded this, you will receive a 429 error with the `Retry-After` header.
L232:   * Please note that if your orders are consistently filled by trades, you can continuously place orders on the API. For more information, please see cite49†Spot Unfilled Order Count Rules .
L233:   * The number of unfilled orders is tracked for each account.
L234: ## Data Sources
L235: 
L236:   * The API system is asynchronous, so some delay in the response is normal and expected.
L237:   * Each endpoint has a data source indicating where the data is being retrieved, and thus which endpoints have the most up-to-date response.
L238: 
L239: These are the three sources, ordered by least to most potential for delays in data updates.
L240:   * Matching Engine - the data is from the Matching Engine
L241:   * Memory - the data is from a server's local or external memory
L242:   * Database - the data is taken directly from a database
L243: 
L244: Some endpoints can have more than 1 data source. (e.g. Memory => Database) This means that the endpoint will check the first Data Source, and if it cannot find the value it's looking for it will check the next one.
L245: ## Request Security
L246:   * Each endpoint has a security type indicating required API key permissions, shown next to the endpoint name (e.g., cite50†New order (TRADE) ).
L247:   * If unspecified, the security type is `NONE`.
L248:   * Except for `NONE`, all endpoints with a security type are considered `SIGNED` requests (i.e. including a `signature`).
L249:   * Secure endpoints require a valid API key to be specified and authenticated.
L250:     * API keys can be created on the cite51†SPOT Test Network†testnet.binance.vision upon logging in with your Github account.
L251:     * Both API key and secret key are sensitive. Never share them with anyone. If you notice unusual activity in your account, immediately revoke all the keys and contact Binance support.
L252:   * API keys can be configured to allow access only to certain types of secure endpoints.
L253:     * For example, you can have an API key with `TRADE` permission for trading, while using a separate API key with `USER_DATA` permission to monitor your order status.
L254:     * By default, an API key cannot `TRADE`. You need to enable trading in API Management first.
L255: Security type  | Description
L256: --- | ---
L257: `NONE`  | Public market data
L258: `TRADE`  | Trading on the exchange, placing and canceling orders
L259: `USER_DATA`  | Private account information, such as order status and your trading history
L260: `USER_STREAM`  | Managing User Data Stream subscriptions
L261: ### SIGNED Endpoint security
L262: 
L263:   * `SIGNED` endpoints require an additional parameter, `signature`, to be sent in the `query string` or `request body`.
L264: #### Signature Case Sensitivity
L265: 
L266:   * HMAC: Signatures generated using HMAC are not case-sensitive. This means the signature string can be verified regardless of letter casing.
L267:   * RSA: Signatures generated using RSA are case-sensitive.
L268:   * Ed25519: Signatures generated using Ed25519 are also case-sensitive
L269: Please consult cite52†SIGNED request example (HMAC) , cite53†SIGNED request example (RSA) , and cite54†SIGNED request example (Ed25519) on how to compute signature, depending on which API key type you are using.
L270: ### Timing security
L271:   * `SIGNED` requests also require a `timestamp` parameter which should be the current timestamp either in milliseconds or microseconds. (See cite55†General API Information )
L272:   * An additional optional parameter, `recvWindow`, specifies for how long the request stays valid and may only be specified in milliseconds.
L273:     * `recvWindow` supports up to three decimal places of precision (e.g., 6000.346) so that microseconds may be specified.
L274:     * If `recvWindow` is not sent, it defaults to 5000 milliseconds.
L275:     * Maximum `recvWindow` is 60000 milliseconds.
